grants.description: Verify your identity against your existing Universal Credit claim
grants.purpose: To confirm you are an existing Universal Credit claimant and link this application to your claim

grants.description: Allow DWP to request and review medical evidence from your GP or healthcare providers
grants.purpose: To gather evidence of your health condition for the Work Capability Assessment

grants.description: Share your information with the independent assessment provider (currently Maximus/IAS) for the Work Capability Assessment
grants.purpose: The assessment provider needs this information to conduct your Work Capability Assessment

grants.description: Consent to attend a Work Capability Assessment, which may be face-to-face, by telephone, or by video
grants.purpose: The healthcare professional needs to assess your capability for work through an assessment

grants.description: Allow DWP to notify you of the assessment outcome and any changes to your Universal Credit payment
grants.purpose: You will receive a decision letter explaining the outcome and your right to request mandatory reconsideration

grants.description: Consent to periodic reviews of your health condition and work capability
grants.purpose: Your LCWRA status may be reviewed periodically to ensure you continue to meet the criteria

revocation.mechanism: You can withdraw consent by contacting DWP through your Universal Credit account or calling the UC helpline. You can also refuse to attend an assessment.
revocation.effect: Withdrawing consent or not attending your assessment will result in your LCWRA application being rejected. Your standard Universal Credit will continue but without the additional LCWRA element.

delegation.agent_identity: GOV.UK AI Agent on behalf of Universal Credit claimant
delegation.limitations: Agent CANNOT attend the Work Capability Assessment on your behalf - you must attend in person or arrange an approved representative. Agent CANNOT sign mandatory reconsideration requests - you must provide your own signature. Agent CAN help you gather evidence, prepare for assessment, understand decisions, and submit supporting documents. Agent CANNOT provide medical opinions or diagnosis.
